title: Zero denominator returns NOT_DEFINED instead of 0% or an infinite rate
risk: A ratio is computed over an empty denominator and published as 0% or as an unbounded number, so a campaign with no delivery is reported as a total failure or as an infinite success.
preconditions: Namespace gov-kpi-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the metric is computed by the real reporting code over fixtures/offline/governance.json kpi_dataset and never copied from the dashboard payload.

Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z with the reporting window 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z as a half-open interval; the stored aggregate is recomputed independently from the raw counter rows.
kpi_edge.zero_denominator supplies zero impressions and zero clicks with three valid leads, so the denominator is genuinely empty while the numerator is not.
The reporting layer is configured to return a typed undefined state rather than a numeric fallback.

steps.action: Compute the three ratios over the empty denominator
steps.expected: Each returns the typed undefined state NOT_DEFINED with the reason (zero denominator), and the numerator value is still reported for context.

steps.action: Confirm that no numeric fallback is produced
steps.expected: None of the three metrics reports 0, 0.0, 100% or an unbounded value; the stored row holds a null value and an explicit reason code.

steps.action: Add one impression so the denominator becomes 1
steps.expected: The metric is then computed normally, proving the undefined state came from the empty denominator rather than from a broken metric.

steps.action: Attempt to divide by zero through the API and the dashboard
steps.expected: Both refuse with the same typed state; no exception text, NaN or Infinity reaches the display.

assertions: An empty denominator yields NOT_DEFINED and never 0%, 100%, NaN or Infinity on any surface.
The numerator is still visible so the operator sees that work happened while the denominator is empty.
The metric becomes computable as soon as a denominator row exists, so the undefined state is a property of the data and not of the metric code.
No API response, log line or dashboard payload leaks a raw division error.
forbidden: Adding 1 to the denominator to avoid division by zero.
Filling the empty denominator with a carried-over value from the previous window.
evidence: Aggregate rows for the three metrics showing the null value and the reason code.
API and dashboard payloads showing the typed undefined state.
Follow-up computation after a denominator row is added.
cleanup: Delete gov- aggregate rows and the added denominator test row after export.
automation: The reporting service and the metric dictionary run as real code under test over the frozen KPI dataset; the dashboard is a consumer whose displayed value must equal the independently recomputed value. Waits are condition-based on the stored aggregate row, metric values are never supplied as inputs, and no vendor boundary is involved in the arithmetic.
